blocks.title: Multifactor Authentication and Password Concepts comparison
Multifactor Authentication and Password Concepts exam shortcuts
items: Example: Two knowledge factors still count as one factor category.
Knowledge + inherence are different factor types.
Example: User enters password and scans fingerprint.
Phone authenticator + security key → both are HAVE
Two possession methods are not two distinct factor categories.
Need strongest phishing resistance → SECURITY KEY / PASSWORDLESS
FIDO2-style keys and passkeys resist credential phishing better than passwords.
Example: User signs in with a hardware security key.
Passwords keep getting reused → PASSWORD MANAGER
Generate and store unique passwords per site.
Example: The vault creates a different random password for every service.
Question focuses on location → SOMEWHERE YOU ARE
Location can be used as a contextual authentication factor.
Example: Access is allowed only from an approved country.
blocks.example: First determine whether the scenario is asking who the user is, what they can do, how they authenticate, or how privileged access should be controlled.

questions.q: A user authenticates with a password and a fingerprint. Does this qualify as MFA?
choices: Yes, because the factors are know + are
No, biometrics cannot be used for MFA
questions.explanation: A password is something you know and a fingerprint is something you are, so they are different factor types.

questions.q: A user provides a password and a PIN. Does this count as true MFA?
choices: No, both are something you know
Yes, because there are two credentials
Yes, because a PIN is possession
No, because passwords cannot be used in MFA
questions.explanation: Password and PIN are both knowledge factors.

questions.q: A physical USB/NFC authenticator is used for strong phishing-resistant login. Which implementation is this?
questions.explanation: Security keys are physical cryptographic authenticators and can provide phishing-resistant authentication.

questions.q: An authenticator app on a smartphone generates one-time codes. Which implementation is this?
questions.explanation: A software authenticator is a soft token.

questions.q: A company wants users to stop reusing the same password across websites. Which tool is most directly helpful?
questions.explanation: Password managers generate and store unique passwords for each service.

questions.q: A user signs in with a passkey and no memorized password. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Passwordless authentication does not require a traditional memorized password.

questions.q: Access is allowed only when the user is physically located in an approved country. Which factor is being used?
questions.explanation: Location is the 'somewhere you are' factor.
